problem: Prior VLN knowledge graphs (ConceptNet, Scene-KG) are static and entity-centric, and event-based attempts (VLN-EventKG) are text-only or simulator-derived, so agents lack procedural, action-linked, visually grounded priors for coarse-grained instructions and long-horizon reasoning.
motivation: Human navigation is predictive and driven by episodic memory, whereas parametric VLN agents react to visual patterns and wander under ambiguous instructions like 'find the sink'. Real-world indoor tour videos contain abundant room-to-room transition knowledge that can be mined into explicit, interpretable multimodal event memory.
key_idea: Mine 320+ hours of YouTube indoor tour videos into a multimodal event knowledge graph (YE-KG) and inject retrieved textual events and future video features into an existing VLN planner via coarse-to-fine retrieval and a cross-attention fusion module (ASTFF).
insight: Ablations show both text (instruction augmentation) and visual (ASTFF) branches contribute, with both together best (val-unseen REVERIE SR 53.37 -> 54.90 text-only / 53.95 visual-only -> 55.33 both). Event nodes drive SR gains while scene-only nodes hurt SR (0 event, 3 scene: 52.51), and the best mix is 2 events + 1 scene. Gains are mostly in SR/RGS with SPL flat or slightly lower, i.e. priors encourage exploration of relevant areas at some path-length cost; gains are modest (~1-2 points).
method: YE-KG video mining: 3,471 real-estate tour videos (>320 h) sampled at 0.5 FPS, outdoor frames filtered, CLIP zero-shot room labeling, adjacent same-label frames merged, min-entropy representative frame per segment; clips between consecutive representative frames form room-to-room event clips (~83k, mean ~11.6 s).

Semantic text generation: LLaVA-NeXT-Video describes each clip; GPT-4 refines/verifies it and labels it Event-0 (clear source room -> action -> target room) or Scene-1 (static scene description only, kept as context nodes).
Graph construction: nodes are event texts with ViT clip features (>86k nodes, >83k edges); directed edges link temporally adjacent clips from the same video.

Coarse retrieval: encode the instruction with Sentence-Transformer, FAISS top-K search over event descriptions, then expand along causal edges to get the subgraph G_sub (once per instruction, 3.92 ms).
Fine retrieval: at each step the panoramic feature queries G_sub for top-n visually similar events, and their causal successor nodes give future-scene features (0.02 ms per step).
Instruction augmentation: retrieved event texts are appended to the instruction after an <EVENT> token.

ASTFF: single-layer Knowledge-Guided Transformer block (8 heads, d=768, 4.73M params) with the current observation as Q and retrieved video features as K/V, learnable modality type tokens, residual + LayerNorm, feeding the backbone policy (GOAT for REVERIE/R2R, ETPNav for R2R-CE).

setting.backbone: GOAT (REVERIE, R2R) and ETPNav (R2R-CE) with ASTFF + retrieval; LLaVA-NeXT-Video, GPT-4, CLIP, ViT used offline for KG construction
setting.model_size: ASTFF adds 4.73M params; KG features 487 MB
setting.training_data: Standard VLN pre-training (MLM, SAP, CFP, +OG for REVERIE) with EnvEdit augmentation and two synthetic corpora, 300k iterations; fine-tuning 50k iterations; YE-KG from 3,471 YouTube videos (>320 h, ~83k clips)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (REVERIE, R2R); topological waypoints with low-level continuous control (R2R-CE via ETPNav)

results: Adding YE-KG to GOAT lifts REVERIE val-unseen SR from 53.37 to 55.33 and test-unseen SR from 57.72 to 59.55, and R2R val-unseen SR from 77.82 to 79.01. On R2R-CE it improves ETPNav val-unseen SR 59 -> 61 and SPL 49 -> 50. SPL is roughly flat on REVERIE (slightly lower).
limitations: Gains are modest (~1-2 SR points) and SPL does not improve on REVERIE, with slightly longer paths
Only tested as an add-on to GOAT/ETPNav; real-world validation is qualitative only, with no quantitative results
KG quality depends on LLaVA/GPT-4 descriptions and CLIP room labels from real-estate videos, whose domain may be biased
